title: Order a drink
capability: You can order a drink and say thank you.

lines: Let's learn how to order a drink.

steps.title: Bitte means two things.
steps.body: Please. And also you're welcome.

steps.goal: Order a drink, then say thanks.

title: Say hello
capability: You can greet anyone, at any time of day.

lines: Let's learn how to greet anyone.

steps.title: Guten does all the work.
steps.body: Guten Tag, Guten Morgen. Same first word every time. Learn the pattern once, not each greeting from scratch.

steps.goal: Greet him in the morning, then say bye when he leaves.

title: Introduce yourself
capability: You can introduce yourself and ask their name right back.

lines: Let's learn how to introduce yourself.

steps.title: "Und du?" needs no translating.
steps.body: It already is the English.

steps.en: Now say it yourself, the way you'll actually say it.

steps.goal: She goes first. Give your name right back.

turns.them: Hallo! Ich heiße Anna. Und du?

title: Ask the price
capability: You can ask what something costs, and understand the answer.

lines: Let's learn how to ask what something costs.

steps.title: Kostet already sounds like "costs".
steps.body: German and English are cousins. Spot the resemblance and you'll guess more words than you memorize.

steps.title: Der means 'the'.
steps.body: Was kostet der Kaffee? -- der just points at 'the coffee'. You'll see it in front of lots of things.

steps.q: Three of these are greetings. Which one isn't?
Ask first. Then say what you honestly think.

steps.goal: Ask the price, then say what you honestly think of it.

title: Eat out
capability: You can order food, react to how good it is, and ask for the bill.

lines: Let's learn how to order food and ask for the bill.

steps.title: Speisekarte = Speise + Karte.
steps.body: Food-card. Spot the pieces, guess the rest.

steps.title: Die is another way to say 'the'.
steps.body: You saw der with der Kaffee -- die Rechnung uses die instead. Same word, 'the', just changes with the noun.

steps.goal: Say thanks for the menu, react to the food, then ask for the bill.

title: Count to five
capability: You can count to five.

lines: Let's learn how to count to five.

steps.title: Vier sounds like "four" if you squint.
steps.body: Some German and English number words are secretly related. Listen for it as you count.

steps.goal: Finish the count.

title: Ask someone's name, formally
capability: You can ask a stranger's name, and know when "du" would be rude.

lines: Let's learn how to ask a stranger's name.

steps.title: Sie always gets a capital letter.
steps.body: Even mid-sentence. That capital S is your visual cue you're being formal.

steps.q: Three of these are numbers. Which one isn't?
Which one do you use with your boss?
Which one do you use with a friend?

steps.goal: Ask her name formally, then give yours.

title: Count to ten
capability: You can count to ten.

lines: Let's learn how to count to ten.

steps.title: Sechs and "six" are the same word.
steps.body: Different clothes, same word. German numbers borrow from the same family English does.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Finish the count.

title: Give your phone number
capability: You can give a phone number, and take one too.
proof: Meine Telefonnummer ist null sechs zwei drei.

lines: Let's learn how to give your phone number.

steps.title: Telefonnummer = Telefon + Nummer.
steps.body: You already knew both halves.

steps.en: Dial it out: meine Telefonnummer ist null sechs zwei drei.

steps.goal: Give your number.

turns.en: Good day! What is your name?

opts.de: Meine Telefonnummer ist null sechs zwei drei.

title: Count to twenty
capability: You can count to twenty, using a trick instead of more memorizing.
proof: Elf, zwölf, dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, zwanzig.

lines: Let's learn how to count to twenty.

steps.title: Elf and zwölf break the rule on purpose.
steps.body: Only two numbers in the whole system don't fuse. Learn these two exceptions and every number after 12 follows the pattern you already know.

steps.q: Three of these are numbers. Which one isn't?

steps.de: Elf, zwölf, dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, zwanzig.
steps.en: Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, twenty.

steps.goal: Confirm the number.

title: Buy bread
capability: You can buy bread or cake, and ask for a piece.

lines: Let's learn how to buy bread.

steps.title: Möchte already means 'would like'.
steps.body: Ich möchte ein Stück Kuchen. Use it any time you want something, politely.

steps.title: Ein means 'a' or 'an'.
steps.body: Ein Stück Kuchen -- a piece of cake. You'll see it change to eine with some words later; for now just know it means 'a'.

steps.en: Dial out: a piece of cake.

steps.goal: Buy something from the bakery.

title: Ask if they have it
capability: You can ask a shop if they have milk or cheese.

lines: Let's learn how to ask a shop what they have.

steps.title: Haben Sie is one chunk.
steps.body: It always means 'do you have,' asked politely. Use it as one piece, not two.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Ask the shop what they have.

title: Buy meat and sausage
capability: You can ask for fresh meat or sausage, by weight.

lines: Let's learn how to buy meat and sausage.

steps.title: Frisch never changes.
steps.body: Ist das Fleisch frisch? Frisch stays frisch, no matter what it describes.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Buy fresh meat or sausage.

title: Ask about the price
capability: You can ask for more or less of something, and say if it costs too much.

lines: Let's learn how to ask for more or less.

steps.title: Teuer and billig are opposites.
steps.body: Das ist teuer. Das ist billig. Same sentence shape, opposite meaning.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Say something is too expensive and ask for less.

title: Buy fruit and vegetables
capability: You can ask for fruit or vegetables, and say how much you need.

lines: Let's learn how to buy fruit and vegetables.

steps.title: Wie viel is one chunk.
steps.body: It always asks for an amount, together, not two separate words.

steps.goal: Ask for fruit or vegetables, and say if it's enough.

title: Ask if they have strawberries
capability: You can ask if a market has something, using a new way to ask.

lines: Let's learn how to ask if something is there.

steps.title: Gibt es is another way to ask.
steps.body: Haben Sie and Gibt es both ask if something's available. Gibt es works without saying 'you'.

steps.goal: Ask if the market has strawberries.

turns.en: Hello! What are you looking for?

turns.them: Erdbeeren? Die sind heute leider aus. Aber ich habe frische Zitronen.
turns.en: Strawberries? Sorry, those are out today. But I have fresh lemons.

title: Say what you'd like to try
capability: You can say you'd like to try something, and point out which one.

lines: Let's learn how to say what you'd like to try.

steps.title: Das hier and das da point.
steps.body: Das hier means this one, close to you. Das da means that one, further away.

steps.title: Probieren becomes probiere for 'I'.
steps.body: Drop the -en, add nothing: probieren -> ich probiere. Most verbs work this way for 'I'.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Say you'd like to try something.

turns.en: Would you like to try some?

turns.them: Hier, bitte. Das hier oder das da?
turns.en: Here you go. This one or that one?

title: Pay for it
capability: You can pay for what you bought, by cash or by card.

lines: Let's learn how to pay for it.

steps.title: Zusammen means all of it, at once.
steps.body: Bezahlen Sie zusammen? Paying for everything as one, not item by item.

steps.title: Bezahlen becomes bezahle for 'I'.
steps.body: Same drop-the-en pattern as probieren: bezahlen -> ich bezahle.

steps.goal: Say how you'll pay.

turns.them: Das macht zehn Euro. Bar oder Karte?
turns.en: That's ten euros. Cash or card?
Good. Do you need a bag?

title: Ask for a bag
capability: You can ask for a bag, and say if you need an extra one.

lines: Let's learn how to ask for a bag.

steps.title: Brauchen is a plain, useful verb.
steps.body: Ich brauche... I need... Use it for almost anything you're asking for.

steps.en: Dial out: Ich brauche eine Tüte.

steps.goal: Ask for a bag.

turns.them: Ist das alles, oder brauchen Sie noch etwas?
turns.en: Is that everything, or do you still need something?

title: Finish your shopping day
capability: You can say you're all done, and say a warm goodbye.

lines: Let's learn how to finish up and say goodbye.

steps.title: Bis bald is a warm goodbye.
steps.body: Not just tschüss. Bis bald means see you soon, said kindly.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

steps.goal: Say you're done and say goodbye warmly.

title: Ask what time it is
capability: You can ask what time it is and tell the time using numbers you already know.

lines: Let's learn how to ask what time it is.

steps.title: Es ist + a number + Uhr tells the time.
steps.body: Wie spät ist es? Es ist drei Uhr. Just put the number you already know before Uhr.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.

lines: Now, a real conversation. You check your watch: it's 3:00.

steps.goal: Your watch says 3:00. Tell her.

turns.them: Ich muss jetzt los. Bis später!
turns.en: I have to go now. See you later!

title: Talk about your schedule
capability: You can say when your appointment is.

lines: Let's learn how to talk about your schedule.

steps.title: Um goes right before the time.
steps.body: Ich habe einen Termin um drei Uhr. Um plus a number plus Uhr says exactly when.

steps.en: Do you have an appointment tomorrow?

steps.de: Ich habe einen Termin um drei Uhr.

cards.en: Do you have an appointment tomorrow?

steps.sentence: Ich habe jetzt einen Termin, bis später!
steps.sentenceEn: I have an appointment now, see you later!
steps.context: Maya texts you right before she runs into a meeting.

steps.goal: Say when your appointment is.

turns.them: Guten Tag! Haben Sie einen Termin?
turns.en: Hello! Do you have an appointment?

turns.them: Gut. Ist heute oder morgen richtig?
turns.en: Good. Is today or tomorrow right?

title: Ask when your appointment is
capability: You can ask when your appointment is.

lines: Let's learn how to ask when your appointment is.

steps.title: Nächste means 'next.'
steps.body: Nächste Woche. Nächste plus a time word says 'next ___.'

steps.goal: Ask when your appointment is.

turns.them: Guten Tag! Wann ist Ihr Termin?
Oh, heute ist leider voll. Passt nächste Woche?
turns.en: Oh, today is unfortunately full. Does next week work?

title: Say which day you have a shift
capability: You can say which day you have a shift.

lines: Let's learn how to say which day you work.

steps.title: Am goes right before the day.
steps.body: Ich habe am Montag Schicht. Am plus a day tells you when.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.
I have a shift on Monday.

steps.de: Haben Sie am Freitag eine Schicht?
steps.en: Do you have a shift on Friday?

cards.en: I have a shift on Monday.

lines: Now, a real conversation. Your schedule: a shift on Monday, not Friday this week.

steps.goal: Your shift is Monday, not Friday. Tell her.

turns.them: Hallo! Haben Sie heute eine Schicht?
turns.en: Hello! Do you have a shift today?

title: Name the rest of the week
capability: You can name the other days of the week.

lines: Let's learn the rest of the week.

steps.title: German weekdays hide a number.
steps.body: Montag is day 1, Dienstag is day 2, Mittwoch is day 3. The names follow the week's own order.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.
I have a shift on Tuesday.

steps.de: Haben Sie am Mittwoch eine Schicht?
steps.en: Do you have a shift on Wednesday?

cards.en: Do you have a shift on Tuesday?
I have a shift on Wednesday.
I have a shift on Thursday.

lines: Your colleague wants your whole week.

steps.goal: Say which other days you work.

opts.de: Ja, ich habe am Dienstag Schicht.
opts.en: Yes, I have a shift on Tuesday.

title: Say you're free on Sunday
capability: You can say Sunday is your day off, and talk about the weekend.

lines: Let's learn how to say you're free.

steps.title: One sentence, all seven days.
steps.body: Maya Does My Duty, Feels Super Sleepy. Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag -- the first letters spell it out.

steps.en: Dial out: I have Sunday off.
Do you work on the weekend?

cards.en: Do you work on the weekend?

lines: Now, a real conversation. Your day off this week: Sunday.

steps.goal: Your day off is Sunday. Tell her.

turns.en: Do you work on the weekend?

title: Say your shift type and hours
capability: You can say if you have an early or late shift, and when it runs.
proof: Ich habe Fruehschicht, von sieben bis fuenfzehn Uhr.

lines: Let's learn how to say your shift type.

steps.title: Von...bis... frames any time range.
steps.body: Von sieben bis fuenfzehn Uhr -- from seven to fifteen (3pm). Works for shifts, opening hours, anything with a start and an end.

steps.en: Do you have the late shift?

steps.de: Meine Schicht ist von sieben bis fünfzehn Uhr.

cards.en: Do you have the late shift?

cards.de: Meine Schicht ist von sieben bis fünfzehn Uhr.
cards.en: My shift is from seven to fifteen.

steps.goal: Say your shift type and hours.

turns.en: Do you have the early shift today?

title: Say how long your shift lasts
capability: You can ask how long something takes, and answer approximately in hours.

lines: Let's learn how to ask how long something takes.

steps.title: Wie lange...dauert...? asks about duration.
steps.body: Wie lange dauert die Schicht? -- how long does the shift last? Swap Schicht for anything: a break, a bus ride, a meeting.

steps.en: Tap them in order, before Maya gets there.
How long does the shift last?

cards.en: How long does the shift last?

lines: Now, a real conversation. Your shift today: about eight hours.

steps.goal: Your shift is about eight hours. Tell her.

turns.them: Wie lange dauert Ihre Schicht heute?
turns.en: How long does your shift last today?

title: Say you're running late
capability: You can apologize for running late, say how many minutes, and give traffic as the reason.

lines: Let's learn how to say you're running late.

steps.title: Stau! can be a whole sentence.
steps.body: Germans often just say the reason alone -- Stau! explains everything. No need for a full sentence.

steps.q: What do you text your colleague?

steps.goal: Apologize and say how many minutes late you are.

title: Confirm or correct what you heard
capability: You can confirm if something is right, correct it if it's wrong, and say you understood.

lines: Let's learn how to confirm or correct something.

steps.title: Richtig and falsch are opposites.
steps.body: Ist das richtig? -- Nein, das ist falsch. One word flips the whole answer.

steps.goal: Confirm what your colleague says about your schedule.

turns.en: So you have the early shift, right?

turns.them: Und die Schicht ist von sieben bis fünfzehn Uhr, oder?
turns.en: And the shift is from seven to fifteen, right?
